Testing for Prediabetes and Diabetes
Unfortunately, type 2 diabetes is frequently not diagnosed until complications appear. Therefore, 
testing to detect prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in asymptomatic adults is important. There is a 
long presymptomatic phase before the diagnosis of type 2 diabetes is usually made and effective

interventions can be utilized to prevent progression from prediabetes to diabetes and to reduce the 
risk of complications. Testing should be considered in all adults at any age with a body mass index 
(BMI) ≥25 kg/m2 and who have one or more of the known risk factors for diabetes listed in Table 
8-1. In those without risk factors, testing should begin no later than age 45. If tests are normal, 
testing should be repeated at 3-year intervals, with considerations of more frequent testing depend­
ing on initial results and risk status (e.g., those with prediabetes should be tested yearly).
